atlas_purpose: Explain vLLM-to-Spyre integration seams from first principles down to exact source lines, while making commit/ref context explicit.

how_to_read.title: Start With Execution Model
how_to_read.details: Read scheduler and attention metadata seams first so every later plugin/KV detail has concrete runtime context.

how_to_read.title: Map Extension Boundaries
how_to_read.details: See how platform registration and platform interface hooks choose worker, model runner, attention backend, and connector components.

how_to_read.title: Trace KV Lifecycle
how_to_read.details: Follow KV allocation, slot mapping, scheduler connector hooks, and connector lifecycle methods end-to-end.

how_to_read.title: Compare Hardware Paths
how_to_read.details: Contrast CUDA paged-attention assumptions with Spyre constraints and torch-spyre runtime maturity constraints.

how_to_read.title: Translate To POCs
how_to_read.details: Use seam evidence to build correctness-first attention backend and KV connector POCs before optimizing performance.

architecture_layers.title: Runtime Scheduling Layer
architecture_layers.summary: Unified prefill/decode scheduling, token budgeting, and request progression semantics.
what_to_verify: No strict prefill/decode phase split in upstream scheduler semantics.
Spyre custom scheduler introduces hardware-specific policy and constraints.

architecture_layers.title: Paged KV Memory Layer
architecture_layers.summary: Block allocation, block tables, slot mapping, and attention backend KV layout contract.
what_to_verify: Attention backend shape/stride contract is explicit and testable.
slot_mapping and block tables drive physical KV reads/writes.

architecture_layers.title: Disaggregation / Transfer Layer
architecture_layers.summary: Scheduler and worker connector hooks orchestrate KV load/save across prefill and decode boundaries.
what_to_verify: Connector lifecycle ordering is clear and instrumented.
Metadata contract includes enough info to map KV blocks correctly.

architecture_layers.title: Plugin / Platform Layer
architecture_layers.summary: Platform registration, platform interface seams, and generation split between vllm-spyre today and next.
what_to_verify: Today stack overrides more internals than next stack targets.
Next stack should converge on upstream extension seams.

architecture_layers.title: Compiler + Device Runtime Layer
architecture_layers.summary: torch.compile path, Inductor hooks, PrivateUse1 backend setup, and runtime fallbacks/limitations.
what_to_verify: Inductor integration points exist and are explicitly patched/registered.
Runtime limitations are identified before claiming production readiness.

badge_legend.label: repo badge
badge_legend.meaning: Which codebase the snippet came from (upstream vLLM, vllm-spyre today, vllm-spyre-next, torch-spyre).

badge_legend.label: commit + ref badges
badge_legend.meaning: Exact commit SHA used for snippet extraction and the local branch/ref for context.

badge_legend.label: Lx-Ly badge
badge_legend.meaning: Precise line range shown in the snippet card and in permalink anchors.

badge_legend.label: sha-not-in-origin warning
badge_legend.meaning: The local commit may not be in currently fetched origin refs; branch permalink is shown for convenience but SHA link stays primary.

global_caveats: Seam extraction uses typed anchors (symbol/literal/contains_all/range); regex anchors are disabled unless explicitly enabled in config.
Inline snippets are extracted from git blobs at local HEAD commit, not the working tree.
Permalink (sha) always points to the pinned commit used for extraction.
Permalink (branch) can move as branch heads update and is for orientation only.
Cross-repo comparisons are meaningful only when version alignment seam confirms dependency band compatibility.

first_principles.title: Prefill vs decode
first_principles.summary: vLLM scheduling is token-progress based, not a hard phase split; this affects chunked prefill and connector semantics.

first_principles.title: Paged KV + slot mapping
first_principles.summary: KV blocks are paged and addressed through block tables and slot mappings; backend correctness depends on these mappings.

first_principles.title: KV connector lifecycle
first_principles.summary: Disaggregated serving relies on scheduler/worker connector hooks and strict metadata consistency.

first_principles.title: Spyre generation split
first_principles.summary: Today path uses custom scheduler/FMS-heavy integration; next path targets upstream seams with smaller custom surface.

steps.text: Implement gather->reference attention->scatter path that respects slot_mapping and block tables before optimizing kernels.
Run prefill+decode comparisons against upstream CPU backend and validate logits/tolerances.
Implement in-memory KVConnectorBase_V1 with explicit metadata and lifecycle logging.
Exercise with disaggregated prefill harness and verify save/load ordering per layer.
Make prefill return host-visible KV outputs and decode consume them without inventing a separate scheduling model.

glossary.definition: Initial prompt processing phase that computes many new tokens and writes the first KV cache entries.
Iterative generation phase that appends new tokens while reusing cached KV for prior context.
KV storage organized into fixed-size blocks to reduce fragmentation and support continuous batching.
Mapping from token positions to physical KV slots/blocks used by attention backends and runners.
Per-request mapping of logical sequence blocks to physical cache blocks.
Connector API for scheduler/worker lifecycle methods to load/save KV across disaggregated boundaries.
Entry-point based mechanism used by vLLM to select platform-specific worker/model-runner/attention integration.
PyTorch device backend registration path used by torch-spyre before dedicated core device-type integration.
